basis.text: A live performance, a DJ or karaoke needs a Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (one performer without amplification who ends by 10 p.m. needs none). Recorded music indoors with no performer needs no entertainment permit, and dancing by patrons needs no permit of its own. Where a permit is needed: further review.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain written confirmation from San Francisco Planning (Zoning Administrator) whether the concept is a bar use requiring CUA or a restaurant use, and clarify the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD license-transfer requirement.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a zoning determination request describing a 40-seat establishment serving beer and wine with limited cooking (small plates) and live entertainment until 1 a.m. Ask: (1) Is this looked up as a bar use under Planning Code § 102, requiring Conditional Use Authorization under § 762 and § 249.60? (2) If it is a bar, must the ABC license be transferred from another bar already inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage SUD, or can the existing Type 41 at this address be retained? (3) If it is a restaurant, does the live entertainment trigger a separate CUA under the nighttime-entertainment rules? State that you need the determination before filing the CUA or committing to a license transfer.

filing_playbook.action: After the DPH plan check is approved and construction is substantially complete, file for the Health Permit to Operate and schedule the pre-opening inspection.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, Location ID (LIN), and federal tax ID. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (FY2026–27; the annual license fee for restaurants and bars is $0 for 2026–28). Ensure a certified food safety manager is on staff. Schedule the final DPH inspection for when the kitchen is complete, all equipment is installed, and hot water and hand sinks are operational. Failed inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks, so walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline is the sum of days to approval for the four approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.conditional_use_authorization), Place of Entertainment or Limited Live Performance permit (45–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.place_of_entertainment_permit), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.health_permit), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days from filing to approval, per catalog:sf.building_permit). These approvals run partly in parallel: the POE and building permit can be filed after the CUA is approved and final, and the health permit is filed after DPH plan check (which is part of the building permit routing) and construction are substantially complete. The CUA is the critical path (6–10 months including pre-application, environmental review, and hearing). The cost range is the sum of city and state government fees for those four approvals: CUA ($3,100–$15,000, higher if construction value is high or no fee waiver applies), POE or LLP permit ($612–$3,800, $2,708 for POE in 2026–27), health plan check and permit ($828 + $470 = $1,298 to $2,500 + $1,000 = $3,500), and building permit ($800–$15,000, percentage of construction valuation). It does not include the cost of purchasing and transferring the ABC Type 42 license (broker fees, license purchase price of tens of thousands of dollars, and ABC transfer fee of $1,000–$1,600), the architect's fees for plans, construction costs, or business setup fees (entity formation, EIN, business registration, seller's permit, food safety certification, RBS training, workers' comp insurance, music licenses). The ABC license transfer timeline (60–150 days per catalog:ca.abc_type_42) runs after CUA approval and is not included in the approval-path timeline above because it is a post-approval step, but it is a prerequisite to opening and serving alcohol. The overall time from CUA filing to opening is realistically 12–18 months if the CUA, POE, ABC transfer, building permit, and health inspections all proceed without delays.

records_summary: 995 Valencia St sits in the NCT-VALENCIA zoning district where restaurants are principally permitted but bars require Conditional Use Authorization. The site is inside the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District, which mandates that any new bar must acquire a liquor license transferred from another bar already located within the SUD. The address currently operates as Sarita's Grill & Beer with an active ABC Type 41 (on-sale beer and wine, eating place) issued November 2023; the records show continuous restaurant use here since at least 1999, including a 2011 CUA approving an upgrade from Type 41 to Type 47. Within 500 ft there are 24 registered food/drink businesses and 9 active on-sale ABC licenses, signaling a commercially dense corridor. Only 3 dated use decisions have been filed within 1,000 ft over the past 10 years (1 approved, 2 withdrawn)—too few to calculate an approval rate—though 74 entertainment permits and licenses have been granted in that radius without discretionary review.
